title: Kansai-Style Nikujaga (Beef & Potato Stew)
subtitle: Sweet Simmered Beef and Onions
description: In Kansai-style Nikujaga, beef is the standard rather than pork. The home-cooked taste is achieved by simmering it sweet and colorful with light soy sauce.

steps.text: Cut the beef strips into bite-sized pieces, quarter the potatoes, cut the onion into wedges, and chop the carrots into irregular bite-sized pieces.
steps.tip: Soaking potatoes in water helps prevent them from falling apart while simmering.

steps.text: Heat oil in a pot and sauté the beef; once the color changes, add sugar and coat well.
steps.tip: Adding sugar first makes the beef more tender.

steps.text: Add the vegetables and stir-fry together, then add 300ml dashi, sake, and mirin, and simmer with a drop-lid for 10 minutes.
Add light soy sauce and simmer for another 8 minutes until the liquid is reduced to 1/3.
steps.tip: Turn off the heat and let sit for 10 minutes to allow flavors to soak in.

clerk_tip: The "beef scraps" in the meat department are the perfect thickness for Nikujaga. Domestic beef scraps are on sale this week.

variations.label: Sweetened for children
variations.note: Increase sugar and mirin by 1 tsp each, and use less ginger and chili pepper.

variations.label: Time-saving (Microwave)
variations.note: Combine ingredients and seasonings in a heat-safe bowl, cover with plastic wrap, and microwave at 600W for 12 minutes.

variations.label: Hearty Portion
variations.note: Add 1 pack of ito konnyaku (konjac noodles) to make it more filling.

title: Kansai-Style Sukiyaki
subtitle: Sear with sugar and soy sauce without using sukiyaki sauce
description: Kansai-style: Sear the beef in beef tallow and season by sprinkling sugar and soy sauce directly onto it. Enjoy with Kujo green onions and yaki-tofu.

steps.text: Melt beef tallow in a pot, spread the beef out, and sear.
steps.tip: The Kansai style is to grill and eat the first slice immediately.

steps.text: Sprinkle with sugar, drizzle with soy sauce, and coat the meat.
Add Kujo green onions, grilled tofu, shirataki noodles, shungiku (garland chrysanthemum), and shiitake mushrooms, then simmer while adjusting the flavor with sake.
steps.tip: No sukiyaki sauce (warishita) is needed as moisture comes out of the vegetables.

steps.text: Dip in beaten egg to eat. Udon noodles are recommended for the finish.

clerk_tip: For beef shoulder loin for sukiyaki, you can consult about the thickness at the service counter in the meat department.

variations.label: Sweetened for children
variations.note: Use more sugar and less soy sauce. Use plenty of eggs.

variations.label: Time-saving (Microwave)
variations.note: No knife needed if you use a pre-cut sukiyaki vegetable set.

variations.label: Hearty Portion
variations.note: Add 2 servings of udon noodles to finish the meal.

ingredients.name: Beef Chuck Eye Roll for Sukiyaki

title: Pork Belly and Daikon Radish
subtitle: Rich sweet and savory simmered dish that goes great with rice
description: A winter classic where the savory flavor of pork belly soaks into the daikon. Use pre-boiled daikon to save time.

steps.text: Cut the daikon into 2cm thick quarter-rounds and the pork belly into 4cm wide pieces.
steps.tip: Microwaving the daikon for 5 minutes cuts the simmering time in half.

steps.text: Sauté pork belly in a pot; once the fat renders, add daikon radish and sauté together.
Add 400ml dashi, sake, sugar, and mirin and simmer for 15 minutes, then add soy sauce and simmer until the liquid is reduced.
Serve in a bowl and sprinkle with green onions.

clerk_tip: The top part of the daikon is sweet and good for simmering. A 1/2 cut from the produce section is perfect for 4 servings.

variations.label: Sweetened for children
variations.note: Increase sugar and mirin by 1 tsp each, and use less ginger and chili pepper.

variations.label: Time-saving (Microwave)
variations.note: Pre-cook the daikon in the microwave; if using a pressure cooker, pressure cook for 5 minutes.

variations.label: Hearty Portion
variations.note: Add 4 boiled eggs and simmer together.

title: Tai no Aradaki (Simmered Sea Bream Scraps)
subtitle: Sweet and savory Akashi/Awaji sea bream
description: A Kansai fish dish of sea bream scraps simmered richly with sake, soy sauce, and sugar. Serving with burdock root is standard.

steps.text: Pour boiling water over the sea bream scraps, then wash off scales and blood in cold water (parboiling).
steps.tip: This is an important prep step to remove odors.

steps.text: Cut the burdock root into 5cm lengths and thinly slice the ginger.
Boil 150ml sake, 100ml water, sugar, and mirin in a pot, then add the fish scraps, burdock root, and ginger.
Simmer with a drop-lid for 10 minutes, then add soy sauce and simmer while spooning the liquid over until glazed.

clerk_tip: Freshly caught sea bream scraps (ara) arrive at the fish department. Aim for morning shopping.

variations.label: Time-saving (Microwave)
variations.note: Ready in 10 minutes with no prep needed if you use sea bream fillets.

variations.label: Hearty Portion
variations.note: Add the yaki-tofu and let it absorb the cooking liquid.

title: Buri Daikon (Simmered Yellowtail & Daikon Radish)
subtitle: Made with fatty winter yellowtail
description: A winter home-cooked dish of winter yellowtail (buri) scraps and fillets simmered with daikon in a sweet and savory sauce. The daikon absorbs plenty of the yellowtail's umami.

steps.text: Cut the daikon into 3cm thick half-moons and pre-boil in rice water for 10 minutes.
Blanch the yellowtail in boiling water and pat dry.
Place daikon, yellowtail, ginger, 400ml water, and sake in a pot and simmer for 10 minutes.
Add sugar, mirin, and soy sauce, then simmer with a drop-lid for 15 minutes.
steps.tip: It tastes even better if left overnight.

clerk_tip: Farmed yellowtail from Kagoshima Prefecture is recommended as it is fatty and holds its shape well when simmered.

variations.label: Time-saving (Microwave)
variations.note: Ready in 12 minutes if you use pre-boiled daikon radish.

variations.label: Hearty Portion
variations.note: Add boiled eggs.

title: Beef Sinew Doteyaki-Style Stew
subtitle: An Osaka flavor simmered until tender with white miso
description: Make the Shinsekai, Osaka specialty 'Doteyaki' at home. Simmer beef tendon and konnyaku in a sweet white miso base.

steps.text: Boil the beef sinew in plenty of water for 10 minutes, drain, rinse with water, and cut into bite-sized pieces.
steps.tip: Parboil and drain to remove scum and excess fat.

steps.text: Tear the konnyaku into pieces and parboil.
Place beef tendon, 800ml water, sake, and ginger in a pot and simmer on low heat for 60 minutes.
steps.tip: If using a pressure cooker, pressure cook for 20 minutes.

steps.text: Add konnyaku, white miso, sugar, and mirin, simmer for 20 minutes until thickened, then top with green onions.

clerk_tip: Domestic beef sinew arrives in the meat department every Tuesday and Friday.

variations.label: Time-saving (Microwave)
variations.note: Pressure cook for 20 minutes + simmer for 10 minutes.

variations.label: Hearty Portion
variations.note: Add daikon to make it hearty.

title: Pork Kimchi Stir-fry
subtitle: Stamina-boosting side dish ready in 10 minutes
description: Just stir-fry pork scraps and napa cabbage kimchi. A quick side dish with an appetizing sesame oil aroma.

steps.text: Season the pork scraps with a little sake and soy sauce.
Heat sesame oil in a frying pan and sauté the pork; once the color changes, add the onions.
Add the kimchi and stir-fry briefly, then season with a little soy sauce.
steps.tip: The secret is not to overcook the kimchi.

steps.text: Serve in a bowl and sprinkle with green onions and toasted sesame seeds.

clerk_tip: The domestic napa cabbage kimchi in the chilled foods section is popular for its mild spice level.

variations.label: Sweetened for children
variations.note: Use half the kimchi and add beaten egg for a milder flavor.

variations.label: Hearty Portion
variations.note: Add one bag of bean sprouts to increase the volume.

title: Chicken Karaage (Japanese fried chicken)
subtitle: Juicy with a ginger soy sauce marinade
description: A classic kids love. Marinated in soy sauce with ginger and garlic, then double-fried for a crispy finish.

steps.text: Cut chicken thighs into bite-sized pieces and marinate for 15 minutes in soy sauce, sake, grated ginger, and garlic.
Mix equal parts potato starch and cake flour to coat.
steps.tip: Using two types of flour makes it crispy and juicy.

steps.text: Fry in 170°C oil for 3 minutes, remove, and let rest for 3 minutes.
Double-fry at 190°C for 1 minute to finish. Serve with lemon.

clerk_tip: On busy days, freshly fried "In-store Fried Karaage" is available at the deli counter at 16:00.

variations.label: Sweetened for children
variations.note: Omit the garlic and use less soy sauce for a sweeter marinade.

variations.label: Time-saving (Microwave)
variations.note: Pan-fry in plenty of oil for 10 minutes instead of deep-frying.

variations.label: Hearty Portion
variations.note: Add chicken breast to double the portion.

title: Fluffy Hamburg Steak
subtitle: A family favorite made with ground meat blend
description: A Western-style classic grilled fluffy with ground meat blend and onions. Make the sauce easily with ketchup and Worcestershire sauce.

steps.text: Finely mince the onion, microwave for 3 minutes, and let cool.
Knead the ground meat blend, onion, panko breadcrumbs, milk, egg, salt, and pepper well, divide into 4 portions, and shape into ovals.
steps.tip: Indenting the center makes it less likely to crack.

steps.text: Sear both sides in a frying pan, then cover and steam on low heat for 8 minutes.
Add ketchup and Worcestershire sauce to the meat juices and simmer down to make a sauce.

clerk_tip: The "Domestic Ground Meat Blend" in the meat section is a 6:4 beef-to-pork ratio, perfect for hamburger steaks.

variations.label: Sweetened for children
variations.note: Add extra ketchup to the sauce. Top with cheese and let it melt.

variations.label: Time-saving (Microwave)
variations.note: Ready in 3 minutes using "Chilled Cheese Hamburger Steaks" that just need heating.

variations.label: Hearty Portion
variations.note: Top with a fried egg for extra volume.

title: Salmon Chanchan-yaki (Salmon & Vegetable Miso Stir-fry)
subtitle: Pan-steamed with miso butter
description: Steam-fry raw salmon, cabbage, onion, and shimeji mushrooms with miso butter. A great way to eat plenty of vegetables.

steps.text: Roughly chop the cabbage, thinly slice the onion, and separate the shimeji mushrooms into small clusters.
Mix the miso, mirin, sugar, and sake to make the miso sauce.
Melt butter in a frying pan, sear the salmon skin-side down, and top with vegetables.
Pour the miso sauce over the top, cover, and steam-fry on low heat for 8 minutes.
steps.tip: Flake the salmon and mix with the vegetables as you eat.

clerk_tip: If you use the deboned raw salmon (mildly salted) from the seafood section, it is safe for children.

variations.label: Sweetened for children
variations.note: Add extra mirin to the miso sauce to make it sweeter.

variations.label: Hearty Portion
variations.note: Add potatoes.

title: Saba no Misoni (Mackerel Simmered in Miso)
subtitle: Ginger-Infused Rice Topping
description: A classic fish dish of mackerel simmered richly with awase miso and ginger. Delicious even when cold, perfect for bento.

steps.text: Score the skin of the mackerel and parboil by pouring boiling water over it.
Boil 150ml water, sake, sugar, mirin, and ginger in a pot.
Place the mackerel skin-side up and simmer with a drop-lid for 5 minutes.
Dissolve the miso into the liquid and simmer for 5 minutes while spooning the sauce over the ingredients.
steps.tip: Add the miso at the end to preserve its aroma.

clerk_tip: The "Chub Mackerel Fillets" in the fish department are already filleted into three pieces, so no prep is needed.

variations.label: Sweetened for children
variations.note: Increase the sugar for a sweet miso finish.

variations.label: Time-saving (Microwave)
variations.note: A 3-minute microwave version using canned mackerel and miso is also possible.

title: Reishabu (chilled pork) salad
subtitle: Refreshing Pork Loin and Mizuna Greens
description: Quickly boil pork shabu-shabu slices and serve with mizuna or tomatoes and ponzu or sesame sauce. Popular year-round.

steps.text: Boil water in a pot, add sake, turn off the heat, and poach the pork one slice at a time at about 80°C.
steps.tip: The secret to a tender finish is not letting it reach a rolling boil.

steps.text: Drain in a colander and let cool naturally (placing in ice water will make it tough).
Cut the mizuna into 5cm pieces, wedge the tomatoes, and julienne the cucumber.
Arrange the vegetables and pork in a bowl and serve with ponzu or sesame sauce.

clerk_tip: For pork loin for shabu-shabu, you can specify thin slices at the meat counter.

variations.label: Sweetened for children
variations.note: Drizzle with plenty of sesame dressing.

variations.label: Hearty Portion
variations.note: Serve over boiled udon for a cold shabu-shabu udon dish.

title: Pork Shogayaki (Ginger Pork)
subtitle: Contains onions so the sauce coats well
description: A classic rice-friendly dish of thinly sliced pork loin seared in a ginger soy sauce glaze. Serve with shredded cabbage.

steps.text: Combine soy sauce, sake, mirin, sugar, and grated ginger to make the sauce.
Lightly coat the pork with potato starch.
steps.tip: The sauce coats the ingredients well.

steps.text: Sauté the pork and onions in a frying pan, then add the sauce and glaze until glossy.
Serve together with shredded cabbage.

clerk_tip: Pre-cut shredded cabbage from the produce section labeled "no washing needed" is convenient for saving time.

variations.label: Sweetened for children
variations.note: Reduce the ginger and add a little honey.

variations.label: Hearty Portion
variations.note: Increase pork to 500g.

title: Chicken and Daikon Taitan (Simmered Chicken & Daikon)
subtitle: Cozy Kansai-Style Simmered Chicken Drumsticks
description: In Kansai, simmered dishes are called "taitan." Simmer chicken drumsticks and daikon elegantly with light soy sauce.

steps.text: Cut the daikon into thick quarter-rounds and microwave for 5 minutes.
Sear the chicken drumsticks until browned.
Add 500ml dashi, sake, mirin, and sugar, then add the daikon radish and simmer for 20 minutes.
Add light soy sauce and cook for another 10 minutes.
steps.tip: Also delicious with boiled eggs.

clerk_tip: Chicken drumsticks are a great value in the meat department's economy packs.

variations.label: Sweetened for children
variations.note: Increase sugar and mirin by 1 tsp each, and use less ginger and chili pepper.

variations.label: Time-saving (Microwave)
variations.note: Pressure cook for 8 minutes.

title: Kitsune Udon
subtitle: Sweet simmered fried tofu and Kansai dashi
description: Kitsune Udon originating from Osaka. Clear kelp and bonito dashi topped with a large piece of sweet and savory simmered fried tofu.

steps.text: Blanch the aburaage (fried tofu) in boiling water to remove excess oil, then cut in half.
Simmer the aburaage (fried tofu) in 150ml water, sugar, soy sauce, and mirin for 10 minutes.
steps.tip: The flavors soak in even more as it cools.

steps.text: Season 600ml dashi with light soy sauce, mirin, and salt to make the udon soup base.
steps.tip: Kansai-style dashi uses light soy sauce for a pale color and a rich aroma.

steps.text: Pour the broth over the boiled udon and top with fried tofu and Kujo green onions.

clerk_tip: Using pre-seasoned "kitsune udon fried tofu" takes the work out of simmering and finishes in just 5 minutes.

variations.label: Time-saving (Microwave)
variations.note: Ready in 5 minutes using seasoned fried tofu and udon soup base.

variations.label: Hearty Portion
variations.note: Top with kamaboko (fish cake) and tenkasu (tempura bits).

title: Oyakodon (Chicken and Egg Bowl)
subtitle: Fluffy and tender with Kujo green onions
description: A rice bowl with chicken thighs and onions simmered in dashi and topped with fluffy egg. The Kansai style uses plenty of Kujo green onions.

steps.text: Cut chicken thighs into bite-sized pieces and thinly slice the onion.
In a small frying pan, bring the dashi, soy sauce, mirin, and sugar to a boil, then simmer the chicken and onion for 5 minutes.
Pour in the beaten egg in two batches and turn off the heat when soft-cooked.
steps.tip: Adding it in two batches makes it fluffy and tender.

steps.text: Place on rice and sprinkle with Kujo green onions.

clerk_tip: Morning-picked Kujo green onions from Kyoto are available in the produce section.

variations.label: Sweetened for children
variations.note: Use more mirin and fewer green onions.

variations.label: Hearty Portion
variations.note: Add one extra egg and increase the amount of chicken.

title: Tanindun (Beef and Egg Bowl)
subtitle: An Osaka-style rice bowl with beef and egg
description: "Tanindun" (Stranger Bowl), which uses beef (or pork) instead of chicken with egg, is a staple in Kansai diners.

steps.text: Cut the beef strips into bite-sized pieces and thinly slice the onion.
Bring dashi, soy sauce, mirin, and sugar to a boil, then simmer the beef and onions.
Bind with beaten egg and serve over rice.
Garnish with mitsuba or green onions.

clerk_tip: The small portion packs of beef strips are the perfect amount for 1-2 servings of a rice bowl.

variations.label: Sweetened for children
variations.note: Increase sugar and mirin by 1 tsp each, and use less ginger and chili pepper.

variations.label: Hearty Portion
variations.note: Extra large rice portion & added soft-boiled egg.

title: Yakisoba with sauce
subtitle: Restaurant-style Pork Scraps and Cabbage
description: Kansai-style home Yakisoba: pan-fry steamed noodles until crispy and finish with Worcestershire and semi-thick sauce.

steps.text: Cut the pork scraps into bite-sized pieces and roughly chop the cabbage.
Pan-fry the noodles without breaking them apart until browned, then remove from the pan.
steps.tip: Searing the noodles first makes them more fragrant.

steps.text: Stir-fry the pork, cabbage, and bean sprouts, then add the rehydrated noodles and toss with sauce.
Top with aonori, red pickled ginger, and bonito flakes.

clerk_tip: The 3-pack yakisoba noodles in the daily foods section noodle corner are convenient as they come with sauce.

variations.label: Sweetened for children
variations.note: Omit the beni shoga and top with a fried egg.

variations.label: Hearty Portion
variations.note: Use 4 packs of noodles and add bean sprouts.

title: Butatama Okonomiyaki (Pork Savory Pancake - Shrimp-free)
subtitle: Fluffy with mountain yam, a Kansai flour-based classic
description: Osaka-style Butatama (Pork Okonomiyaki) made by grilling pork belly on a cabbage-rich batter. Safe for family members with allergies as it contains no shrimp.

steps.text: Mix okonomiyaki flour with water, egg, and grated nagaimo (yam), then add coarsely chopped cabbage and tenkasu (tempura bits).
steps.tip: The secret to fluffiness is not overmixing.

steps.text: Spread the batter in circles on the griddle and top with pork belly.
Once browned, flip over, cover with a lid, and steam-fry for 5 minutes.
steps.tip: Do not press down on them!

steps.text: Top with okonomiyaki sauce, mayonnaise, aonori (dried seaweed), and katsuobushi (bonito flakes).

clerk_tip: Choose okonomiyaki flour labeled "shrimp-free" to avoid seafood extracts.

variations.label: Sweetened for children
variations.note: Use a mild sauce and add mayonnaise to taste.

variations.label: Hearty Portion
variations.note: Sandwich yakisoba inside to make 'Modanyaki'.

title: Takoyaki (octopus balls)
subtitle: Home Takoyaki Party with a Griddle
description: Use a takoyaki maker, a staple in Kansai homes. Add boiled octopus, tenkasu (tempura scraps), and red pickled ginger to a dashi-rich, creamy batter.

steps.text: Mix takoyaki flour, eggs, and water well to make the batter.
steps.tip: Adding dashi makes it even more authentic.

steps.text: Grease the takoyaki pan, pour in the batter, and add boiled octopus, tempura scraps, red pickled ginger, and green onions.
Once the edges set, use a bamboo skewer to rotate 90 degrees at a time to cook into a round shape.
Top with sauce, mayonnaise, aonori (dried seaweed flakes), and bonito flakes.

clerk_tip: Boiled octopus from Akashi and Hokkaido is now available in the seafood department.

variations.label: Sweetened for children
variations.note: Using wieners or cheese instead of octopus is also popular.

variations.label: Hearty Portion
variations.note: Add konnyaku and chikuwa (fish cake) to the ingredients.

title: Akashiyaki (Egg-rich Takoyaki)
subtitle: Dip the fluffy egg batter into the dashi
description: A local specialty of Akashi, Hyogo. Octopus is placed in a soft, egg-rich batter and eaten dipped in warm dashi broth.

steps.text: Make a dipping sauce by seasoning 400ml dashi with light soy sauce, mirin, and salt, then heat it up.
Mix 4 eggs, 300ml dashi, 50g cake flour, and 1 tbsp potato starch to make the batter.
steps.tip: Use potato starch instead of wheat starch.

steps.text: Pour the batter into the takoyaki pan, add the octopus, and gently round them out.
steps.tip: Handle gently as it breaks easily.

steps.text: Arrange on a board and serve with mitsuba leaves floating in the dipping broth.

clerk_tip: Akashiyaki requires plenty of eggs. We recommend making this on days when 10-count egg packs are on sale.

variations.label: Sweetened for children
variations.note: Add extra mirin to the dipping sauce.

title: Kayaku Gohan (Seasoned rice with mixed ingredients)
subtitle: Kansai-style Takikomi Gohan (Mixed Rice)
description: In Kansai, "kayaku" refers to ingredients. Cook rice with chicken, burdock root, carrot, abura-age (fried tofu), and konnyaku using light soy sauce.

steps.text: Wash the rice and soak in water for 30 minutes.
Cut chicken thighs into small pieces, shave the burdock root, and julienne the carrot, fried tofu, and konnyaku.
Add rice, light soy sauce, sake, mirin, and dashi to the rice cooker, then add water up to the 2-cup mark.
Add the ingredients and cook as usual, then let steam for 10 minutes before mixing.
steps.tip: The trick is to place the ingredients on top without mixing them.

clerk_tip: Takikomi-gohan (mixed rice) ingredient sets (burdock and carrot) are also available in the cut vegetable section of the produce department.

variations.label: Time-saving (Microwave)
variations.note: Use a Takikomi-gohan (mixed rice) base to skip the hassle of cutting ingredients.

variations.label: Hearty Portion
variations.note: Double the amount of chicken.

title: Kuri Gohan (Chestnut Rice)
subtitle: Autumn flavors made with glutinous rice
description: An autumn seasonal rice dish using Tanba chestnuts. Adding a little glutinous rice makes it chewy.

steps.text: Wash the regular rice and glutinous rice, then soak in water for 30 minutes.
Soak chestnuts in boiling water for 10 minutes before peeling the outer and inner skins.
steps.tip: Use peeled chestnuts to save time.

steps.text: Put rice, sake, and salt in the rice cooker, adjust the water level, top with chestnuts, and cook.
Once cooked, steam for 10 minutes and sprinkle with black sesame seeds.

clerk_tip: During this season, chestnuts from Tanba and Kyoto are available in the produce section. Frozen peeled chestnuts are also available.

variations.label: Time-saving (Microwave)
variations.note: Use pre-peeled chestnuts to skip the peeling process.

title: Niku Udon (Nikusui-style Beef Soup)
subtitle: Sweet and Savory Beef with Kansai Dashi
description: Kansai-style Niku Udon topped with sweet and savory simmered beef. Remove the noodles to make the Osaka specialty 'Nikusui'.

steps.text: Simmer the beef strips in soy sauce, sugar, and mirin for a sweet and savory flavor.
Make a Kansai-style soup base by adding light soy sauce, mirin, and salt to dashi.
Boil the udon, pour the broth, and top with beef and Kujo green onions.
Add ichimi or shichimi pepper to taste. Swap udon for a soft-boiled egg to make it 'Nikusui' style.

clerk_tip: One packet of udon soup powder makes Kansai-style broth instantly.

variations.label: Sweetened for children
variations.note: Add ichimi chili pepper for adults only.

variations.label: Hearty Portion
variations.note: Top with a soft-boiled egg and tenkasu (tempura bits).

title: Negiyaki (Green Onion Savory Pancake)
subtitle: Enjoy with plenty of Kujo green onions and soy sauce
description: Negiyaki (green onion pancake) originating from Juso, Osaka. Grill with plenty of green onions and beef tendon konnyaku, served with soy sauce and lemon.

steps.text: Make the batter with okonomiyaki flour, water, and egg.
Spread the batter thinly on the griddle and top with plenty of chopped Kujo green onions.
Top with pork belly or simmered beef tendon, pour over a little batter, flip, and cook.
Brush with soy sauce and squeeze lemon over it before eating.

clerk_tip: Using 2 bunches of Kujo green onions gives it a professional restaurant taste.

variations.label: Hearty Portion
variations.note: Top generously with simmered beef sinew.

title: Kasujiru (Sake lees soup)
subtitle: A Kansai winter soup to warm the body with sake lees
description: A winter soup using sake lees from Nada or Fushimi. Filled with salted salmon or pork and root vegetables to warm you to the core.

steps.text: Soak the sake lees in a small amount of dashi to soften.
steps.tip: Heat in the microwave for 20 seconds to make it easier to melt.

steps.text: Cut the daikon and carrots into quarter-rounds, and the aburaage (fried tofu) and konnyaku into matchsticks.
Simmer root vegetables and salted salmon (or pork) in 800ml dashi; once tender, dissolve the sake lees into the pot.
Season with miso and sprinkle with green onions.

clerk_tip: Sake lees are winter-only; sheet-style lees from Nada breweries arrive in the chilled section.

variations.label: Sweetened for children
variations.note: Use less sake lees and more miso. Bring to a boil to thoroughly cook off the alcohol.

variations.label: Hearty Portion
variations.note: Add pork belly to make Pork Kasujiru (Sake Lees Soup).

title: Sembajiru (Mackerel and Daikon Soup)
subtitle: Shio Saba to Daikon no Osaka Shonin no Shiru (Osaka Merchant's Salted Mackerel & Radish Soup)
description: A clear soup of salted mackerel scraps and daikon born in the merchant houses of Semba, Osaka. A dish embodying the spirit of 'shimatsu' (using everything without waste).

steps.text: Cut the salted mackerel into bite-sized pieces and blanch them with boiling water.
Cut the daikon into matchsticks.
Simmer the daikon radish and salted mackerel in kombu dashi, carefully skimming off the foam.
steps.tip: Removing the scum results in a clear broth.

steps.text: Season with light soy sauce and salt, then garnish with julienned ginger and green onions.

clerk_tip: We recommend the fatty Norwegian salted mackerel from the seafood department.

variations.label: Time-saving (Microwave)
variations.note: Save time by replacing kombu dashi with dashi granules.

title: Hearty Tonjiru (pork and vegetable miso soup)
subtitle: Packed with root vegetables; a single bowl makes a full side dish
description: Pork scraps, daikon, carrots, burdock root, konnyaku, and tofu in awase miso. A nutrient-packed one-bowl meal for busy days.

steps.text: Cut the daikon and carrots into quarter-rounds, shave the burdock root, and tear the konnyaku into pieces.
Heat sesame oil in a pot and sauté the pork and vegetables.
steps.tip: Stir-frying adds richness.

steps.text: Add 800ml dashi and simmer for 10 minutes, then add the tofu.
Dissolve the miso into the liquid and sprinkle with green onions.

clerk_tip: No chopping required if you use pre-cut Tonjiru (pork and vegetable soup) vegetables.

variations.label: Time-saving (Microwave)
variations.note: Zero prep with pre-cut Tonjiru (pork and vegetable soup) vegetables.

variations.label: Hearty Portion
variations.note: Add satoimo (taro root).

title: White Miso Ozoni-Style Clear Soup
subtitle: Sweet and mellow with Kyoto white miso
description: A Kyoto New Year's flavor made with white miso. Add round mochi, satoimo (taro), and daikon radish for a mellow taste.

steps.text: Slice the daikon and carrots into rounds; peel and pre-boil the satoimo (taro).
Simmer the vegetables in kombu dashi.
Dissolve in a generous amount of white miso.
steps.tip: Do not let the white miso come to a boil.

steps.text: Add boiled (not toasted) round mochi and top with katsuobushi (bonito flakes).

clerk_tip: Kyoto white miso is available in larger quantities in the dairy/chilled section during winter.

variations.label: Sweetened for children
variations.note: Cut the mochi into small pieces to prevent choking.

title: Napa Cabbage and Pork Belly Mille-Feuille Hot Pot
subtitle: Just layer and simmer for a beautiful presentation
description: Simply layer napa cabbage and pork belly alternately in a pot and simmer with shiro-dashi. A time-saving hot pot with minimal knife work and cleanup.

steps.text: Layer napa cabbage leaves and pork belly alternately, then cut into 5cm widths.
Pack tightly starting from the outer edge of the pot.
steps.tip: Pack them tightly so they don't fall apart.

steps.text: Place shimeji mushrooms in the center and pour in 500ml water and 80ml shiro-dashi.
Cover and simmer for 15 minutes, then serve with ponzu sauce.

clerk_tip: A 1/4 cut of napa cabbage is the perfect amount for a 4-person hot pot.

variations.label: Sweetened for children
variations.note: Use sesame sauce instead of ponzu.

variations.label: Hearty Portion
variations.note: Finish the meal with udon.

title: Chicken Mizutaki (Chicken Hot Pot)
subtitle: With bone-in chicken white broth
description: Mizutaki (Chicken Hot Pot) enjoyed with a white broth simmered from bone-in chicken. Serve with ponzu and momiji oroshi (grated radish with chili).

steps.text: Parboil the bone-in chicken pieces, then boil with 1.5L water and kombu on high heat for 30 minutes.
steps.tip: Boiling over high heat will turn the soup cloudy.

steps.text: Add napa cabbage, mizuna, green onions, shiitake mushrooms, and tofu.
Once cooked through, enjoy with ponzu sauce.
Finish the meal with rice and egg for zosui (rice porridge).

clerk_tip: The chopped chicken mix for mizutaki is bone-in, which makes a rich soup stock.

variations.label: Time-saving (Microwave)
variations.note: Shorten the simmering time by using chicken stock powder.

variations.label: Hearty Portion
variations.note: Add chicken meatballs.

title: Seafood Yose-Nabe (Hot Pot)
subtitle: Hearty with Shrimp, Cod, and Napa Cabbage
description: Yosenabe (Mixed Hot Pot) with plenty of cod, shrimp, chicken, and vegetables. *Contains shrimp (shrimp-free version available).

steps.text: Roughly chop the napa cabbage, green onions, and shungiku (garland chrysanthemum); decoratively carve the shiitake mushrooms.
Heat the yosenabe soup base and add the chicken and the core of the napa cabbage first, as they take longer to cook.
Add cod, shrimp, tofu, and leafy greens and simmer.
Finish the meal with udon noodles.

clerk_tip: For family members with shrimp allergies, we recommend replacing shrimp with chicken meatballs and scallops.

variations.label: No Shrimp (Allergy-Friendly)
variations.note: Omit shrimp and increase chicken thigh and cod. Use a hot pot broth that does not contain shrimp extract.

variations.label: Hearty Portion
variations.note: Add udon noodles to finish the meal.

title: Yudofu (Tofu Hot Pot)
subtitle: With kombu dashi from Sagano, Kyoto
description: A taste of Kyoto: simply warm tofu in kombu dashi. Because it is simple, use high-quality tofu and kombu.

steps.text: Place water and kombu (kelp) in a clay pot and let sit for 30 minutes.
Cut the tofu into large pieces, add to the pot, and warm over low heat.
steps.tip: It is ready to eat when the tofu begins to wobble slightly.

steps.text: Make a dipping sauce with soy sauce, mirin, and bonito flakes.
Enjoy with Kujo green onions, bonito flakes, and ginger as condiments.

clerk_tip: For Yudofu, the slightly firmer "Kyoto-Style Momen (Cotton)" tofu is recommended over silken tofu.

variations.label: Hearty Portion
variations.note: Add mizuna and cod to make it a hot pot style.

title: Oden (Kanto-style Stew)
subtitle: Kansai-style features beef tendon in a light dashi
description: In Kansai, it is also called "Kanto-daki." The Kansai style is to add beef tendon to a light dashi made from kombu and bonito.

steps.text: Cut the daikon into 3cm thick rounds and pre-boil; boil the eggs and peel them.
Parboil the beef sinew and thread onto skewers.
Season 1.2L of dashi with light soy sauce, mirin, and salt, then simmer the daikon radish, eggs, beef tendon, and konnyaku.
Add the fish cakes, thick fried tofu, and chikuwa, then simmer on low heat for 20 minutes.
steps.tip: Add the fish cakes at the end so they do not over-expand.

clerk_tip: Find the oden starter sets in the daily foods aisle near the fish cakes. Kansai-style dashi base is also available.

variations.label: Time-saving (Microwave)
variations.note: 30 minutes using an oden starter set and oden base.

variations.label: Hearty Portion
variations.note: Add potatoes and octopus.

title: Mizuna and Aburaage no Taitan (Simmered Mizuna & Fried Tofu)
subtitle: Crunchy mizuna greens with shiro-dashi
description: A staple Kyoto Obanzai dish. The key is to cook the mizuna greens quickly to keep them crunchy.

steps.text: Cut the mizuna into 5cm lengths and the aburaage into strips.
Boil 200ml dashi, shiro-dashi, and mirin in a pot, then simmer the abura-age (fried tofu) for 2 minutes.
Add the mizuna stems first, then the leaves, and simmer briefly.
steps.tip: Do not overcook the mizuna.

steps.text: Serve in a bowl along with the simmering liquid.

clerk_tip: Mizuna from Kyoto and Shiga is at its most delicious in winter.

variations.label: Hearty Portion
variations.note: Add the chikuwa.

title: Komatsuna and Abura-age (Deep-Fried Tofu) Nibitashi
subtitle: Dashi-infused greens ready in 5 minutes
description: An everyday side dish of komatsuna and abura-age lightly simmered in dashi. Perfect for meal prep.

steps.text: Cut the komatsuna into 4cm lengths and thinly slice the abura-age.
Bring 200ml dashi, light soy sauce, and mirin to a boil.
Add the aburaage (fried tofu), komatsuna stems, and leaves in that order and simmer for 2 minutes.
Turn off the heat and let cool to absorb the flavors.

clerk_tip: Komatsuna is rich in iron and calcium, making it highly recommended for growing children.

variations.label: Time-saving (Microwave)
variations.note: Microwave in a heat-safe container at 600W for 3 minutes.

title: Dashimaki Tamago (Dashi-Seasoned Omelet)
subtitle: Kansai-style is fluffy with plenty of dashi
description: Kansai-style dashimaki (rolled omelet) contains no sugar and is juicy with plenty of dashi. Serve with grated daikon.

steps.text: Add 80ml dashi, light soy sauce, mirin, and salt to 4 eggs and mix.
steps.tip: Mix as if cutting through the egg whites.

steps.text: Lightly grease a tamagoyaki pan with oil, pour in 1/4 of the egg mixture at a time, and roll.
Shape using a bamboo rolling mat.
Cut into portions and serve with grated daikon radish.

clerk_tip: On busy days, we also recommend the "Kyoto-style Dashimaki (rolled omelet)" from the deli counter.

variations.label: Sweetened for children
variations.note: Add 2 tsp of sugar for a sweet tamagoyaki (Japanese omelet).

title: Hijiki Ni (Simmered Hijiki Seaweed)
subtitle: A meal prep staple, rich in iron
description: A staple side dish of me-hijiki, carrots, fried tofu, and soybeans simmered in a sweet and savory sauce. Great for filling bento boxes.

steps.text: Rehydrate the hijiki in water for 15 minutes, then drain.
Cut the carrots and abura-age (fried tofu) into thin strips.
Sauté in oil, then add 200ml dashi, sugar, soy sauce, and mirin and simmer.
Add the soybeans and simmer until the liquid is gone.

clerk_tip: Me-hijiki is in the dried goods aisle, and boiled soybeans are in the canned goods aisle.

variations.label: Sweetened for children
variations.note: Increase sugar and mirin by 1 tsp each, and use less ginger and chili pepper.

title: Kinpira Gobo (Braised burdock root & carrot)
subtitle: Spicy kick with sesame oil and chili pepper
description: A staple side dish of burdock and carrots sautéed in a sweet and savory sauce. Sprinkle with plenty of sesame seeds.

steps.text: Shave the burdock root and julienne the carrots.
steps.tip: Do not soak the burdock root in water for too long.

steps.text: Sauté in sesame oil.
Add sugar, soy sauce, mirin, and sake, then sauté and simmer until the liquid is gone.
Sprinkle with toasted sesame seeds.

clerk_tip: You can skip the prep by using a pack of pre-cut boiled burdock root.

variations.label: Sweetened for children
variations.note: Make it sweet without chili peppers.

variations.label: Hearty Portion
variations.note: Add lotus root.

title: Potato Salad
subtitle: Home-style flavor with cucumber and ham
description: A classic potato salad combining fluffy potatoes with cucumber, carrots, and ham.

steps.text: Peel and cut the potatoes, microwave for 6 minutes, and mash.
steps.tip: Sprinkle with a little vinegar while hot to help the flavors blend.

steps.text: Thinly slice the cucumber and massage with salt; slice the carrot into ginkgo-leaf shapes and microwave.
Cut the ham into strips.
Once the excess heat has dissipated, toss everything with mayonnaise, salt, and pepper.

clerk_tip: The value 4-pack loin ham in the daily dairy section is a great deal.

variations.label: Hearty Portion
variations.note: Add boiled eggs.

title: Chawanmushi (Savory Egg Custard)
subtitle: Classic Shrimp and Ginkgo Nut
description: A gentle steamed dish made with dashi and egg. Contains shrimp, chicken, kamaboko (fish cake), shiitake mushrooms, and mitsuba. *Contains shrimp (can be made with chicken only).

steps.text: Mix 2 eggs, 300ml dashi, light soy sauce, mirin, and salt, then strain.
steps.tip: Strain for a smooth texture.

steps.text: Place chicken, shrimp, kamaboko (fish cake), and shiitake mushrooms in a bowl and pour in the egg mixture.
Steam on high heat for 2 minutes, then on low heat for 12 minutes.
steps.tip: Use low heat to prevent air bubbles from forming.

steps.text: Top with mitsuba to finish.

clerk_tip: For family members with shrimp allergies, make 'Chicken Chawanmushi' by omitting shrimp and increasing chicken tenderloin.

variations.label: No Shrimp (Chicken Chawanmushi)
variations.note: Omit shrimp and double the chicken thigh. Check that the kamaboko is labeled shrimp-free.

variations.label: Time-saving (Microwave)
variations.note: Microwave in a heat-safe cup at 200W for 8 minutes.

title: Chicken Chawanmushi (Savory Steamed Egg Custard, shrimp-free)
subtitle: Safe for family members with allergies
description: Chawanmushi (savory steamed egg custard) made with chicken, shiitake, and kamaboko instead of shrimp. The gentle dashi flavor remains the same.

steps.text: Mix 2 eggs, 300ml dashi, light soy sauce, mirin, and salt, then strain.
Place chicken, kamaboko (fish cake), and shiitake mushrooms in a bowl and pour in the egg mixture.
Steam on high heat for 2 minutes, then on low heat for 12 minutes.
Top with mitsuba to finish.

clerk_tip: Choose kamaboko that does not list "shrimp" in the ingredients.

variations.label: Time-saving (Microwave)
variations.note: Microwave in a heat-safe cup at 200W for 8 minutes.

title: Fluffy Shrimp and Egg Stir-Fry
subtitle: Chinese-style side dish ready in 10 minutes
description: A Chinese-style side dish of fluffy stir-fried peeled shrimp and eggs. *Contains shrimp (can be substituted with chicken tenderloin).

steps.text: Rub the peeled shrimp with potato starch and salt, then rinse and pat dry.
Mix chicken stock powder and a little milk into the eggs.
Sauté the shrimp and remove; scramble the eggs into large, soft curds.
Return the shrimp to the pan, scatter green onions, and drizzle with sesame oil for aroma.

clerk_tip: For those with shrimp allergies, you can make this the same way using thinly sliced chicken breast.

variations.label: No Shrimp (Chicken Breast)
variations.note: Use thinly sliced chicken breast instead of shrimp.

title: Sweet & Savory Sautéed Sweet Potato and Pork
subtitle: Popular autumn side dish for kids
description: An autumn side dish children love, featuring sweet potatoes like Naruto Kintoki and pork pieces stir-fried in a sweet and savory sauce.

steps.text: Cut the sweet potato into 1cm thick half-moons and microwave for 4 minutes.
Coat the pork scraps with potato starch.
Sauté the pork and sweet potatoes in a frying pan, then coat with soy sauce, sugar, and mirin.
Sprinkle with toasted sesame seeds.

clerk_tip: Naruto Kintoki sweet potatoes from Tokushima are very sweet and perfect for stir-fries.

variations.label: Sweetened for children
variations.note: Increase sugar and mirin by 1 tsp each, and use less ginger and chili pepper.

variations.label: Hearty Portion
variations.note: Increase the amount of pork.

title: Mushroom Takikomi Gohan (Mixed rice)
subtitle: Autumn aroma with 3 types of mushrooms
description: An autumn seasonal rice dish made with shimeji, maitake, and shiitake mushrooms combined with fried tofu and cooked in dashi.

steps.text: Wash the rice and soak in water for 30 minutes.
Break the mushrooms into pieces and cut the aburaage (fried tofu) into thin strips.
Add rice, white dashi, and sake to the rice cooker, adjust the water level, top with ingredients, and cook.
Steam for 10 minutes, mix, and garnish with mitsuba (Japanese parsley).

clerk_tip: Maitake mushrooms have a strong aroma and become the star of takikomi gohan (seasoned rice).

variations.label: Hearty Portion
variations.note: Add the chicken thighs.

steps.text: Heat the chilled cheese hamburger steak in its bag in the microwave (or boiling water) for about 3 minutes as directed.
Plate the "Ready-to-eat 10-item Cut Salad" and cherry tomatoes, then serve with the hamburger steak.
Scoop the smooth silken tofu into a small bowl with a spoon and add a dash of soy sauce if desired to complete a 3-dish set meal!

clerk_tip: Get everything in 30 seconds by moving from the Ham & Sausage section (Z4) to the adjacent Salad section (Z5) in front of the deli! Don't forget to use your ¥50 off hamburger steak coupon.

subtitle: Just layer and steam for 7 minutes! A nutrient-packed main dish with sweet sesame sauce that gets kids to eat plenty of vegetables.
tags: Hearty portion that satisfies even Ken

steps.text: Roughly chop tender Hyogo cabbage and spread half of it across the bottom of a frying pan.
Spread and layer thin slices of domestic pork belly, top with the remaining cabbage, bean sprouts, and mushrooms, sprinkle with 2 tbsp sake, cover, and steam over medium heat for 7 minutes.
Serve with a generous drizzle of mild "Sweet-Style Roasted Sesame Sauce"! For kids, sprinkling some corn on top makes it even more popular.

clerk_tip: Grab the bargain cabbage at the Produce Entrance (Z1) and head straight for the pork belly in Meat (Z3)! For kids who dislike sour ponzu, "sweet sesame sauce" is a surefire hit.

Top the 10-ingredient salad mix with plenty of sweet corn, and serve on a plate with mayonnaise or sesame dressing.

Place smooth silken tofu and Hokkaido small-bean natto in small bowls, then pour hot water over the low-sodium fresh miso soup to complete an elegant Japanese set meal.

Skim the surface and simmer for 4 minutes, then add the chopped komatsuna and cook for 1 minute to finish!

clerk_tip: Buna-shimeji mushrooms can be pulled apart by hand, making them perfect for saving time! Adding udon to the leftover broth is also delicious.

title: [Kansai Specialty, 8 min] Warm Beef and Mizuna Kyoto-Style Nikusui Udon
subtitle: Kansai-style dashi made from bonito and kombu warms the soul! An easy bowl using frozen Sanuki udon.

steps.text: Put water and the "Nikusui Base" in a small pot, bring to a boil, and briefly simmer the beef strips.
Add microwave-thawed frozen Sanuki udon, and just before turning off the heat, top with chopped mizuna for a crisp finish.

clerk_tip: By omitting udon and adding silken tofu, it becomes Osaka Namba's famous 'Nikusui Tofu'—perfect for a low-carb late-night snack!

title: [Low Sodium / Japanese] 5-Kind Kyoto Obanzai Platter with Fresh Yuba & Oboro Tofu Set
subtitle: For couples who want to enjoy a variety of seasonal vegetables in small portions. An elegant, restaurant-style dinner without using heat.

steps.text: Arrange a 5-item Kyoto Obanzai assortment colorfully on a plate.
Place Kyoto-processed raw yuba (tofu skin) for sashimi and oboro tofu in a small bowl, add a few drops of low-sodium soy sauce from a squeeze bottle, and enjoy the sweetness of the soybeans.

clerk_tip: Making many types of simmered dishes is hard for a two-person household, but with our in-store handmade Obanzai (Kyoto-style side dish) platter, you can enjoy 5 varieties with zero food waste!

title: [12 min with pre-boiled daikon] Kagoshima Yellowtail Teriyaki-Style Buri Daikon
subtitle: Buri Daikon (Yellowtail and Daikon) usually takes 40 minutes, but using "Domestic Pre-boiled Daikon" gets the flavor soaked to the center in just 12 minutes!

steps.text: Quickly blanch the yellowtail fillets in boiling water to remove any fishy odor.
Place domestic pre-boiled daikon, yellowtail, shiro-dashi, mirin, and a little soy sauce in a pot, cover with a drop-lid, and simmer over medium heat for 10 minutes until glazed.
Top with boiled komatsuna (mustard spinach) for a colorful, authentic Buri Daikon (simmered yellowtail and radish)!

clerk_tip: The "Pre-boiled Daikon (Cut for Buri-Daikon)" from the produce/daily section is tender to the core, so flavors soak in well even with short simmering times and less seasoning, helping to reduce salt.

title: [Boneless / 10 min] Pan-Seared Mild Salted Silver Salmon & Kyoto-Style White Miso Soup Set
subtitle: Deboned for peace of mind for children and seniors! A comforting Kansai dinner table with sweet white miso and silken tofu.

steps.text: Place the 'Boneless Silver Salmon Fillets' on a frying pan lined with parchment paper and cook for 4 minutes per side until fluffy (cleanup is easy—just discard the paper!).
Warm the silken tofu and frozen spinach in a small pot, then stir in mild white miso to make a mellow miso soup.

clerk_tip: Deboned silver salmon is a hidden gem that is easy for children to eat by themselves and can be put directly into bento lunch boxes the next morning.

title: [Weekend Feast] Bigeye Tuna Sashimi & Crispy-Soft Deep-Fried Tofu with Yuzu Ponzu
subtitle: Cymbal Retail's signature Tuna Sashimi served with fragrant Atsuage (deep-fried tofu) toasted until crispy

steps.text: Slice the bigeye tuna block into bite-sized pieces and arrange on a plate with the mizuna greens.
Toast the atsuage for 5 minutes until crispy, then serve with grated daikon radish and fragrant yuzu ponzu sauce.

clerk_tip: We can also slice it to your preferred thickness at the fish counter! The citrus aroma of yuzu ponzu provides plenty of satisfaction even with reduced salt.
